title: Micro Pilot Activation Cheatcards - Rapid Iter
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact set of cheatcards for sellers + SEs to spin up 7–14 day micro-pilots that prove Redwood Inference value quickly. The emphasis is on low friction, short lead time, clear success metrics, and deterministic handoffs to Dedicated/Private if the pilot proves out.

When to use this doc:
- Prospect expresses interest but needs actual throughput/latency/cost data with their prompts
- Platform teams want an operational sanity-check before committing to capacity
- Pilot incumbent comparison where time-to-evidence matters more than breadth

One-line seller pitch (30s):
"Run a focused 1–2 week micro-pilot with Redwood that demonstrates a production-grade inference path — we’ll validate latency, per-token unit cost, and quality on your canonical prompts so you have measurable economics and a migration-ready config."

Micro-pilot formats (pick one):
1) Live API smoke test (fastest) — connect to hosted Redwood API, run 1–3 canonical prompts, verify latency and output quality.
2) Batch-run evaluation (best for embeddings/large volumes) — upload a representative batch, run at expected concurrency to measure throughput and cost.
3) Mini-tenant on Dedicated node (when isolation or predictable throughput required) — 7-day reserved slot with preconfigured model variant and autoscale knob.

Standard timeline (example, 10 business days):
Day 0: Kickoff call (30m) — agree success metrics, data, security boundaries.
Day 1: SE config + credentials provisioned (hosted or dedicated).
Day 2–3: Smoke runs + sample outputs, initial fixes.
Day 4–8: Load runs and metric collection (latency distributions, p95/p99, throughput, token cost).
Day 9: Review results and next-step recommendations.
Day 10: Executive summary delivered, motion to pilot conversion (Reserved capacity quote / Private deployment plan / Longer PO Cx).

Success metrics (pick top 3 for each pilot):
- Latency: p95 < target-ms (customer-defined) and p99 within fallback tolerance
- Cost: per-token unit cost vs incumbent baseline (show % delta)
- Quality: pass rate on canonical prompt set (human-rated or metric threshold)
- Reliability: error rate < 0.1% during steady-state load
- Operational: ability to run within customer network constraints (for Private)

Minimal technical checklist (hosted API):
- Customer provides 10–20 canonical prompts or sample data (anonymized if needed).
- SE creates a redwood API key scoped to pilot org and route; set rate limits to safe defaults.
- Model variant selection: pick 1 primary and 1 fallback (e.g., vicuna-13b-clamped, quantized-4bit)
- Observe expected sequence length distribution; ensure KV-cache warms before load tests.
- Logging + traces: enable request-level trace_id and token-cost headers for evaluation.
- Budget guardrails: set hard quota to avoid runaway costs.

Quick payload example (copy for SE):
- POST /v1/generate
- Headers: Authorization: Bearer <pilot-key>, X-Trace-Id: <uuid>
- Body: {"model":"chosen-model","input":"<canonical prompt>","max_tokens":128,"stream":false} 
(Adjust keys to match SDK)

Demo script (5–8 min flow for customer meeting):
1) One-liner: objective of the pilot and the metric we’ll prove.
2) Live send of 3 canonical prompts (explain expected output).
3) Show latency numbers in real time (avg/p95 updated).
4) Show cost estimate calculation for 10k requests/month baseline vs measured; call out savings/overhead.
5) Quality check: show 2–3 side-by-side outputs vs incumbent model or baseline.
6) Ask for immediate feedback and confirm go/no-go for extended validation.

Objection quick-responses (cheatcard snippets):
- "We’re worried about latency at scale." → "We’ll run a scaled traffic window to measure p95/p99 — if we miss, we’ll test routing to a lower-precision quantized model and show the delta live."
- "Security / data residency concerns." → "Start with hosted isolated pilot keys and PII-filtered prompts; for production we offer VPC/private deployment and KMS integration. We can include an NDA addendum for test data."
- "How do we compare apples-to-apples on cost?" → "We’ll run your canonical prompt set and produce a per-output unit cost with the same sequence length assumptions used by your incumbent. We also provide a spreadsheet that projects 6/12 month unit economics with and without caching/batching improvements."

Measurement & reporting template (what SE hands back):
- Pilot scope: format, model variant, sample size, duration.
- Raw metrics: request count, avg token count, avg latency, p95, p99, errors, cost tokens, $ cost.
- Quality notes: pass/fail % on canonical prompts, sample outputs (3–5 highlighted).
- Recommendations: route to Dedicated? Recommend quantization? Suggested next-phase contract size.

Hand-off checklist to Sales Ops / AE
- Final report PDF + raw metrics CSV uploaded to shared pilot tracker.
- Decision recommendation: convert to reserved capacity / expand hosted usage / plan private deployment.
- Pricing ask: initial 3-month ramp discount, if converting within 30 days apply credit.
- Legal: confirm SOW terms and billing account are in place.

Internal quick links (copy/paste into Slack)
- "Pilot kickoff: @se-team please provision pilot key for ACME Corp; scope: hosted API, model X, 7 days; sample prompts uploaded to pilot tracker JIRA-PRJ-987."

Operational risks + mitigations
- Risk: Unexpected token surge raises cost. Mitigation: hard quota, early abort on 2x projected gamma.
- Risk: Output quality not representative. Mitigation: require canonical prompt set and define success thresholds up front.
- Risk: Soc compliance / PII exposure during pilot. Mitigation: scrub data, run on Private if un-scrubbable, request an NDA clause.

Conversion triggers (things to push for during results review)
- Stable p95/p99 within target and quality pass rate ≥ threshold.
- Clear unit-cost delta vs incumbent or clear path to parity with quantization/caching.
- Customer engineering buy-in: SE reports < 2 integration blockers.

Sample emails (two-line templates)
- To SE: "Please provision pilot key for <customer> — 7-day hosted pilot, model <X>, sample prompts attached. Timeline: kick off tomorrow."
- To customer POC: "Thanks — running the first smoke tests now. Expect a brief results summary in 48 hours and full report by day 10."

Slide deck skeleton (4 slides) — copy into a 1-page slide:
1) Objective + success metrics
2) Pilot config + sample prompts + expected outputs
3) Topline metrics (latency/cost/quality) + visual charts
4) Recommendation & next steps (convert -> reserved capacity / private deployment / continue testing)

Open questions for product/research: (to be resolved before finalizing pilot script)
- Which model variants should be pre-approved for micro-pilots to reduce gating?
- Fast way to enable KV-cache warming for low-volume pilots?
- Canary policies for auto-fallback when a pilot exceeds latency SLOs?

Notes to SEs: Keep the pilot narrow. Demonstrate a measurable property (latency, cost, or quality) rather than trying to solve every integration issue. Low friction + fast evidence = higher conversion.

End of cheatcards.
